weather_report:
Late morning in Kirribilli feels cool and clean, the harbor wearing a soft pewter sheen as cloud thickens toward midday. A light band of rain looks set to drift through early afternoon, then the sky should loosen into broken cloud later, letting through brief, silvery light before evening. It won’t be a sunny day so much as a day of small mercies: a few bright gaps, then back to grey. UV stays modest for winter, edging up only when the sun peeks, and visibility will be good though the headlands will look gently smudged.

It’s a gentle, slightly damp sort of day. Wear layers and a light waterproof, closed shoes, and keep a compact umbrella or hood handy. If you’re out now, run a few errands or take a short harborfront stroll before the showers; when the rain arrives, tuck into a quiet cafe by a window, answer messages, and watch the ferries trace pale wakes. As the clouds break later, reward yourself with a brief foreshore walk or a quick ferry roundtrip, catching those fleeting patches of blue without lingering long in the wind.
